s1.syndrome_frame: Recurring skin eruptions with vesicles and bullae, starting at birth, with a waxing and waning course, and involving the face, trunk, and extremities
salient_findings: Hyperkeratotic plaques with distinct borders and annular appearance
Vesicles and bullae on the face, trunk, and extremities
key_facts: Born to healthy, nonconsanguineous parents
Normal growth and development for age and sex
Unremarkable family medical history
Initial exam showed multiple areas of erythema, vesicles, and bullae
Vital signs were within normal ranges
Mucous membranes not affected
Skin-punch biopsy revealed hyperkeratosis and bullae formation within the epidermis
Direct immunofluorescence results were unremarkable
Genetic testing revealed a heterozygous variation c.482T>C (p. L161P) in KRT1
Later developed thickened, brown, corrugated plaques and palmoplantar hyperkeratosis

shortlist.label: Epidermolytic hyperkeratosis
shortlist.why_kept: Hyperkeratosis and bullae formation within the epidermis on skin-punch biopsy, and genetic testing revealed a heterozygous variation in KRT1

shortlist.label: Epidermolysis bullosa simplex
shortlist.why_kept: Recurring skin eruptions with vesicles and bullae, starting at birth, with a waxing and waning course

shortlist.label: Darier disease
shortlist.why_kept: Hyperkeratotic plaques and palmoplantar hyperkeratosis, with sparse inflammatory cells in the superficial dermis

shortlist.label: Hailey-Hailey disease
shortlist.why_kept: Family history of similar skin condition is not present, but clinical presentation of vesicles and bullae is similar

shortlist.label: Palmoplantar keratoderma
shortlist.why_kept: Later development of thickened, brown, corrugated plaques and palmoplantar hyperkeratosis
